items.title: Al Gallodoro interviewed by Monk Rowe, Oneonta, New York, December 28, 2005
items.q: And I said, “Bob,” I says, “you play nice, you get a good sound, but man your high notes are so flat.” And this went on night after night.

ctx.x: He played Selmer also. And I said, “Bob,” I says, “you play nice, you get a good sound, but man your high notes are so flat.” And this went on night after night. I said, “Let me try your horn.” I apologized. I said, “It’s not you, Bob, it’s the horn.” They were flat. They were known to be flat, some of the old cigar cutter. They were known to be flat. Then they made them, not in tune but they made them sharp. They didn’t go right there to pitch you know. I spoke to Marcel Mule about that. He says I know they’re…
When you were playing for these shows at that time, in New Orleans, was it a segregated audience at the time?
